rationale:
Our group selected the Logistic regression model for predicting customer
churn based on its performance during stratified 5-fold
cross-validation.

The selected model achieved a mean cross-validation F1 score of
0.4701. We used F1 as our primary evaluation
metric because it balances precision and recall, helping us identify
customers at risk of leaving while limiting incorrect predictions.

We also considered the variation in F1 scores across validation folds,
the number of false negatives, and performance differences between
New and Established customers.

False negatives are particularly important because they represent
customers who actually churned but were predicted to stay. These
customers could be missed by retention campaigns.

We considered model complexity and interpretability when making our
decision. The model was selected using development data only,
without inspecting the final test results.

Although cross-validation provides evidence of generalization,
performance may differ on unseen customers, especially because
the dataset is synthetic.
